clue.text: Drink with little hesitation, so get fatter!

parts.note: stout is a dark beer, a drink
er is the small noise of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A dieting joke: have a drink and pause, and you will put on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Stouter is the comparative of stout, meaning plumper or heavier in build.

clue.text: Digging can be tiring

explanation.surface: Excavation work can wear you out.
explanation.definitionFit: To sap is to dig a trench toward an enemy position; sapping strength is wearing someone out.

clue.text: Boss is through with the episcopate

parts.note: over means finished, as in 'the match is through'
a see is a bishop's diocese, the seat of the episcopate

explanation.surface: A church manager is finished dealing with the bishops.
explanation.definitionFit: To boss workers is to supervise and direct them, the verb sense of superintending.

clue.text: Rows involving joiners

explanation.surface: Arguments among carpenters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' looks like quarrels but means ranks of seats; 'joiners' is not carpenters but people who tie things together.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiers are ranks set one above another, and people who tie knots or bindings join things together.

clue.text: Rubicund character of some importance

parts.note: rubicund means ruddy-faced, red
a letter is a character of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A ruddy-faced person who is quite a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-letter day is a memorable, significant one, from saints' days printed in red in calendars.

clue.text: Stays, but desires to move

indicators.note: the letters of desires are made to move into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone remains in place even though they long to go elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to live or remain there, a synonym of stay.

clue.text: Once again put to sleep without point

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the sleep word goes round the point

parts.note: rest is sleep or repose
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: An animal is put down a second time, with no reason given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means 'outside', so REST is wrapped around E.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset something is to set or place it again, a repeated putting.

clue.text: New Testament account

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made afresh in a different order

explanation.surface: A reference to the Gospels as a narrative of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Testament' reads as the Bible; 'New' is the anagram signal for TESTAMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement is a written or spoken report of facts, an account.

clue.text: Settle the down-payment

explanation.surface: Pay the first instalment and close the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment settles as a layer laid down, and a sum paid in advance secures a purchase.

clue.text: Skilled worker getting more depressed about the Left

indicators.note: about means the sadder word goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: sadder means more depressed, unhappier
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A craftsman grows gloomier over left-wing politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddler is a craftsman who makes and repairs saddles and harness.

clue.text: Page respecting nurse's claim

parts.note: re means concerning or respecting
to tend is to nurse or look after

explanation.surface: A page boy considers a nurse's assertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend is to claim falsely, as to pretend to the throne is to lay claim to it.

clue.text: Gave way and took photographs

explanation.surface: Someone broke down and also took pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope that snapped broke under strain; a photographer snaps shots with a camera.

clue.text: Playing tennis-it's demanding

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved around in play

explanation.surface: A tennis match that proves exhausting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone insistent keeps pressing their demand and will not take no for an answer.

clue.text: Quiet trainee making a stand

parts.note: to ease is to quieten or calm
L is a learner, shown by the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A silent apprentice takes up a position.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a frame that holds a painting or board upright, a stand.

clue.text: Some of the more menacing rebels get the bird

indicators.note: some of signals that only a portion of these words is used

explanation.surface: The most threatening insurgents are hissed off stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get the bird' looks like being booed; 'get' is a link word and 'the bird' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The grebe is a diving water bird with lobed toes.

clue.text: No-one thanks a fellow for turning up and calling out

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: no gives NO and one gives I, the Roman numeral
ta is British informal for thanks
cove is old British slang for a man or fellow

explanation.surface: Nobody thanks a man for arriving and shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'for turning up' reverses the whole string NOITACOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Evocation is the act of summoning or calling forth, as spirits are called up.

clue.text: Where to pull a hundred trees out

parts.note: to tow is to pull
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of trees are put out of order

explanation.surface: A logger asks where to drag a hundred felled trees.
explanation.walkthrough: TOWCESTER is a market town in Northamptonshire, England, known for its racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The bare 'Where' stands for a place name, this town being the location wanted.

clue.text: This could well give some edge to the news broadcast

definitions.text: This could well give some edge

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Something that adds bite to a news programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests radio but scatters the letters of TO THE NEWS.
explanation.definitionFit: A whetstone is a sharpening stone used to put an edge on blades.

clue.text: Talk of the devil and run!

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, so a name for the devil
a course is a run, as a race or path

explanation.surface: Speak of the devil, then flee!
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the saying 'talk of the devil'.
explanation.definitionFit: A discourse is a formal talk or written treatment of a subject.

clue.text: Exercises control over charges

explanation.surface: Someone in authority managing people's accusations.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct is to manage and control; a judge directs, or charges, a jury.

clue.text: Like the gentleman receiving junk mail

indicators.note: receiving means the title word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: sir is the title of a gentleman

indicators.note: junk as a verb means to scrap, so the letters of mail are broken up

explanation.surface: A man getting unwanted advertising post.
explanation.definitionFit: Similar means alike or resembling, as 'like' does in comparisons.

clue.text: An old book to piece together

parts.note: a bit is a piece

explanation.surface: Assembling an antique volume from fragments.
explanation.walkthrough: Tobit is a book of the Apocrypha in the Old Testament canon of some churches.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobit is a book of the Apocrypha, part of the ancient scriptures.

clue.text: Set time allowed for dressing

parts.note: a band is a set or group
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A fixed period allowed for getting changed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandage is a strip of material used to dress a wound.

clue.text: Persons in the wrong environment, and suffering as a result

indicators.note: in places the persons word within the legal wrong
environment says the wrong surrounds the persons as its setting

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men are persons

explanation.surface: People placed in an unsuitable setting are unhappy because of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong environment' reads as a bad setting; TORT, the legal word for a civil wrong, surrounds MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe mental or physical anguish, extreme suffering.

clue.text: Dance music for 27 to some degree

parts.note: the answer at 27 means strange, and rum is British slang for strange
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Music for an odd dance, up to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban dance and the music written for it.

clue.text: He'll take no alcohol-may order tea in bars

indicators.note: may order suggests the letters are put into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A teetotaller might ask for tea in pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstainer refrains from drink altogether, a teetotaller.

clue.text: Fish caught in an Arcadian glen

indicators.note: caught in signals letters held within these words

explanation.surface: A fish taken in a pastoral valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' looks like a noun but is the verb, to angle.
explanation.definitionFit: To angle is to fish with rod and line.

clue.text: Moving article on prison

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the article sits on top of the prison word

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a jail is affecting.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and about, in motion.

clue.text: Giving a name to one's business

explanation.surface: Naming one's company.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone something names them; a calling is a vocation or trade.

clue.text: Striking fashion causing shock

parts.note: out means on strike, as workers who are out
rage is a craze or fashion, 'all the rage'

explanation.surface: A startling style causes a scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is strong shocked indignation at something.

clue.text: Foreign holy man needing cattle-grazing

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man
a range is open land where cattle graze

explanation.surface: A visiting monk needs pasture for his herd.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange in its older sense means alien or from another country.

clue.text: 7? That's serious

explanation.surface: A question about the answer at 7, then an assurance it means business.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 refers to the answer at 7 down, meaning a down-payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest money is a pledge paid to secure a deal, and an earnest person is sincere and grave.
